newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen gaining on bank buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen gaining on bank buying.

text.p: The Thai market should post modest gains on Thursday on expected foreign buying of large capitalised bank stocks, analysts said.
The stock index rose 3.27 points on Wednesday to close at 716.89 points. The SET 50 gained 0.45 points to 53.98.
"Net foreign buying has been over five billion baht so far this month, and it's been very consistent" said Jim Landi, head of research at Vickers Ballas.
Though most investors expect first quarter results will be poor, some foreigners believe that the market's downside is now limited, analysts said.
"The (finance and bank) numbers should start to come in next week and we think they are going to be pretty weak because they have to meet new provisioning requirements," Landi said.
To strengthen the financial sector the central bank recently increased commercial lenders' provisioning requirments.
"The key is that if the numbers come in and they are pretty lousy but the market absorbs them well then it could be a major indicator the market has seen the bottom," Landi said.

The Thai market has lost more than half its value from 1996 highs as Thai economic growth has slowed to its lowest level for a decade, and concerns have heightened surrounding the loan quality of some finance firms.
Shares of troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc are due to resume trading on Thursday after an 11 month suspension with analysts expecting a heavy sell-off.
The stock is included the SET 50 Index of leading stocks.
